candidate.answerReason: The two top labels form an equally likely ordered selection of two distinct physical labels. Each of the 12 possible first labels has exactly 2 favorable partners among the remaining 11 labels.

methods.label: Count the possible partners
methods.explanation:
Treat the two copies of each number as separate physical labels. Whatever two faces the rolls select, random reattachment makes every ordered pair of distinct labels equally likely to occupy those faces. There are \(12\) choices for the label on the first die and \(11\) remaining choices for the label on the second die, giving \(12\cdot11\) equally likely outcomes.

If the first label has value \(x\), the required second value is \(7-x\). For every integer \(x\) from \(1\) through \(6\), this is a different value from \(x\), so both copies of \(7-x\) remain available. Thus each first label has exactly \(2\) favorable partners.

This counts every favorable ordered pair once, according to its first label. Therefore the probability is
\[
\frac{12\cdot2}{12\cdot11}=\boxed{\frac{2}{11}},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\).
